stem: A 20-year-old man notices cola-colored urine starting the day after the onset of a sore throat. It cleared in 3 days, and this is the third such episode in 2 years. His blood pressure is 138/86 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows red cell casts and mild proteinuria. He has no edema, cough or hemoptysis.
oneliner: 20M + cola urine 1 day after each sore throat, 3rd episode + RBC casts + mild proteinuria + no edema or hemoptysis → which biopsy IF finding?
ask: Which renal biopsy immunofluorescence finding is most likely?

options.A: Granular IgG and C3 in subepithelial humps
options.B: Granular subepithelial IgG along the GBM
options.E: Granular IgA deposits in the mesangium

whyNot.A: Post-streptococcal humps; that disease starts **1 to 3 weeks after** a sore throat and rarely recurs, but his bleeding **starts the next day**
whyNot.B: Membranous nephropathy, which causes **nephrotic syndrome** with edema; he has **no edema** and only mild proteinuria
whyNot.C: Anti-GBM disease causes **rapidly progressive** renal failure, not brief episodes that **clear in 3 days**
whyNot.D: Minimal change disease shows no deposits, but it causes **heavy proteinuria and edema** without **red cell casts**

why: **IgA nephropathy** causes recurrent gross hematuria **during or within 1 to 2 days of a mucosal infection**, when increased galactose-deficient IgA1 deposits in the mesangium. **Post-streptococcal GN** has a **1 to 3 week latent period** after pharyngitis. Biopsy shows **mesangial IgA** deposits.

idea.rule: Hematuria at the time of the infection = IgA nephropathy (mesangial IgA); hematuria weeks later = post-infectious GN.
also: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein): same mesangial IgA with purpura, arthralgia, abdominal pain
Post-streptococcal GN: low C3, subepithelial humps, anti-DNase B
Post-streptococcal latency is about 1 to 3 weeks after pharyngitis and 3 to 6 weeks after skin infection
